seo.title: Cube Numbers 1 to 100 Speed Challenge - 3D Math Fluency
seo.metaDescription: Spot all perfect cube numbers between 1 and 100 on an interactive 10x10 math grid. Learn third power exponents and 3D volume concepts.
seo.intro: A cube number (or perfect cube) is the result of multiplying an integer by itself three times (n x n x n = n^3). In geometry, a cube number represents the three-dimensional volume of a cube with whole-number edge lengths. Between 1 and 100, only 4 perfect cubes exist: 1 (1^3), 8 (2^3), 27 (3^3), and 64 (4^3), as the next cube 125 exceeds 100. Spotting these numbers connects exponents with volume geometry.
seo.howToPlay: Scan the grid to find and click the 4 perfect cube numbers up to 100. Correct selections turn green with a checkmark. Non-cubes flash red and deduct 2 seconds from your timer. Find all 4 cubes to win.
seo.teacherNotes: Use base-ten unit blocks to build physical cubes: a 1x1x1 block (1), a 2x2x2 block (8), a 3x3x3 block (27), and a 4x4x4 block (64).

faq.q: What are the perfect cubes up to 100?
faq.a: The four perfect cubes are 1 (1x1x1), 8 (2x2x2), 27 (3x3x3), and 64 (4x4x4).

faq.q: Why is 64 both a square number and a cube number?
faq.a: Because 64 equals 8 squared (8 x 8) and also equals 4 cubed (4 x 4 x 4). In exponential notation, 2^6 = 64.
